name: Andrew
whenBasis: Jesus' ministry, from the fifteenth year of Tiberius (Luke 3:1), AD 28–29, to the crucifixion under Pilate, AD 30 or 33 on reckonings from the gospels' weekday.
summary: A fisherman of Bethsaida, Simon Peter's brother, and a disciple of John the Baptist, who followed Jesus after hearing John call him the Lamb of God. He first found his brother and told him, “We have found the Messiah,” and brought him to Jesus. Called from his nets by the Sea of Galilee, he was one of the Twelve. At the feeding of the five thousand he found the boy with five loaves and two fish.
body: With Philip he brings the Greeks who want to see Jesus. With Peter, James and John he asks Jesus privately on the Mount of Olives when the temple will fall.

later.text: Origen, as quoted by Eusebius, says Andrew was allotted Scythia. The Acts of Andrew (second or third century) has him crucified at Patras in Greece; the X-shaped cross is a later tradition.
He is patron saint of Scotland and of the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople, which counts him its founder.
